note: Adapted from the species description in Sands (1972), originally in English; the alates are based only on a queen and king, whose coloration the original states may be faded. The genus has no soldiers, hence there is no soldier section; measurement tables, figure numbers and locality records are not translated.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The comparisons with A. aneristus and A. apocnetus are given under those species. In A. mansuetus the alate fontanelle is large, the postclypeus more inflated and the mandibular apical tooth shorter; the worker apical tooth is also short, the anterior margins of the first and second marginal teeth of the right mandible are about equal, and the enteric valve seat has a very long neck. In A. pacatus the alate compound eyes and ocelli are large, the apical teeth of both alate and worker are shorter, and the worker enteric valve seat is bilobed and dorsal. A. prosenus is readily recognized by its large size, shallow fontanelle and even pilosity, and its worker has a short midgut–hindgut overlap. The worker abdomen of the present species appears dehiscent.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head capsule pale yellow; pilosity rather sparse but stout and conspicuous, yellow. Postclypeus moderately inflated, Pcl/W 0.25–0.29, Pcl/Rj 2.00–2.34. Mandibular apical tooth long, La/Li 0.80–0.88, Ra/Ri 1.04–1.10; in surface view the subsidiary tooth of the left mandible just clears the molar prominence, La/Li·Lm 16.42–18.61; the first marginal tooth of the right mandible lies distinctly behind the line from the apical tooth to the second marginal tooth, its anterior margin shorter than that of the second marginal tooth, Ra/Ri·Rm 17.30–21.90. Fore tibia slender, Ti/Tw 5.06–5.75; third apical spur distinct, about half the length of the other two. The midgut–hindgut overlap is about twice as long as the width of the midgut at the origin of the Malpighian tubules, and the hindgut reaches half of the Malpighian tubule knot; in the unopened abdomen the enteric valve seat is ventral, the trilobation rather weak, the third lobe smaller, and joined to the second hindgut pouch by a distinct neck; no discernible minute spines were observed on the valve membrane outside the cushions.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head capsule chestnut brown, darker above the ocelli; fontanelle almost as large as the ocellus, slightly raised, short-elliptical, brown; central spot very small, slightly raised, circular, concolorous with the head capsule; postclypeus brown, labrum yellow; frontal groove indistinct, a flat brown crescent; antennae brown. Pronotum and meso- and metanotum brown, the dark transverse sutures very distinct; femora pale brown, tibiae yellowish brown, tarsi yellow. Abdominal tergites and dorsal spiracles brown, ventral spiracles and lateral parts of the sternites pale brown, the median part yellow; cerci pale yellowish brown. Posterior margin of head capsule evenly rounded; ocelli moderate, their distance from the compound eye two thirds of their minimum diameter to the whole minimum diameter; postclypeus weakly inflated, Pcl/W 0.21–0.24, posterior margin arcuate, not evenly rounded, median suture weakly developed. Mandibular apical tooth of moderate length, La/Li 0.67–0.80, Ra/Rj 0.95–1.07; in surface view the subsidiary tooth of the left mandible is remote from the molar prominence; the tip of the first marginal tooth of the right mandible lies slightly behind the line from the apical tooth to the second marginal tooth, the anterior margins of the marginal teeth about equal in length. Meso- and metanotum narrower at the constriction, M/W 0.24–0.28. Cephalic pilosity brown, uneven, without a hair layer.
